title: Web Access authority source extraction for DIS-008 porcine epidemic diarrhoea / PED
disease_name: Porcine epidemic diarrhoea / porcine epidemic diarrhea virus
extraction_method: Codex web-access skill workflow with authority source verification, search discovery, official page/PDF URL checks, and source-first governance routing

authority_sources.title: Porcine epidemic diarrhoea
explicit_dis008_support: WOAH describes PED as a non-zoonotic viral disease of pigs caused by a coronavirus and characterised by watery diarrhoea and weight loss.
WOAH states that PED affects pigs of all ages but most severely neonatal piglets, with morbidity and mortality reaching up to 100% and mortality decreasing with age.
WOAH states that PED is mainly transmitted by the faecal-oral route.
WOAH states that PED is clinically similar to other forms of porcine gastroenteritis and includes anorexia, vomiting, diarrhoea and dehydration.
WOAH states that prevention and management control focus on strict biosecurity and early detection.
WOAH states that there is no specific treatment for PED.
WOAH states that PED is not included in the WOAH List of Diseases, while emerging-disease reporting obligations can apply in the context described by the WOAH Terrestrial Animal Health Code.
limitations: International WOAH disease page; do not use as a substitute for current China-specific reporting, quarantine, culling, movement-control, vaccination, or farm-closure requirements.
Do not convert the no-specific-treatment statement into drug, dose, route, treatment-course, withdrawal-period, MRL, residue, food-safety, or therapeutic protocol conclusions.
Use PED/TGE/gastroenteritis similarity only as a diagnostic-boundary anchor requiring laboratory support, not as a single-cause diagnosis from clinical signs alone.

authority_sources.title: Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea (PED) Technical Note
authority_sources.page_type: US federal animal-health technical note PDF
explicit_dis008_support: USDA APHIS describes PED's pathogenic agent as a coronavirus distinguishable from transmissible gastroenteritis of swine only by laboratory tests.
USDA APHIS states that PED is most serious in neonatal piglets, where morbidity and mortality can be 80 to 100 percent.
USDA APHIS states that PED transmission is fecal-oral and that no vector or reservoir has been implicated in its spread in the technical note.
USDA APHIS states that economic loss occurs through death and production loss, plus vaccination and biosecurity costs.
USDA APHIS states there is no effective treatment other than control of secondary infections.
limitations: US federal technical note; do not use to infer China-specific legal status, reporting, movement controls, quarantine, culling, vaccination schedules, or market rules.

The treatment sentence is a boundary statement only and is not a product-label source; do not infer executable antimicrobial prescriptions, dose, route, course, withdrawal period, MRL, residue, or food-safety conclusions.
Do not extend PED facts to TGEV, PDCoV, rotavirus, ETEC or other enteric diseases without separate disease-specific sources.

supported_claims.claim: WOAH identifies PED as a non-zoonotic viral disease of pigs caused by a coronavirus and characterised by watery diarrhoea and weight loss.
WOAH states that PED affects pigs of all ages but is most severe in neonatal piglets, with morbidity and mortality reaching up to 100% and mortality decreasing as age increases.
WOAH states that PED is mainly transmitted by the faecal-oral route and that prevention and management control focus on strict biosecurity and early detection.
WOAH states that PED is clinically similar to other forms of porcine gastroenteritis and that there is no specific treatment; this supports diagnostic and treatment-boundary use only.
USDA APHIS states that PED's coronavirus agent is distinguishable from transmissible gastroenteritis of swine only by laboratory tests.
USDA APHIS states that PED transmission is fecal-oral and that no vector or reservoir has been implicated in its spread in the technical note.

do_not_extrapolate: Do not generate China-specific reporting, quarantine, culling, movement-control, vaccination schedule, farm-closure, or market-access conclusions from WOAH or USDA pages alone.
Do not convert no-treatment or secondary-infection wording into executable prescriptions, antimicrobial choices, dose, route, course, withdrawal period, MRL, residue, or food-safety conclusions.
Do not diagnose PED from watery diarrhoea alone; clinical similarity to TGE and other porcine gastroenteritis requires laboratory-supported differentiation.
